title: Feelings
about: How we feel: happy, sad, angry, tired, hungry, cold and more. How to say what you love, like, hate, prefer, hope and want.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Про те, як ти себе почуваєш, англійською говорять через «я» + прикметник: I'm cold, I'm hot, I'm hungry, I'm thirsty, I'm tired — а не «мені». It's cold, it's hot — це про погоду чи кімнату. Ще дві пари, які часто плутають: боятися чогось — be afraid of sth (I'm afraid of dogs), сумувати за кимось — miss sb (I miss my grandma). I'm sad for you означає «мені тебе шкода».

rows: I really like pizza. / I like pizza very much.
I very like pizza. / I like very much pizza.
Я більше люблю чай, ніж каву.

items.pattern: love sb / sth · love + -ing
items.meaning: like someone or something very, very much (++)
items.example: I **love** my grandma's apple pie.
more: My little brother **loves** his new puppy.
I **love** reading in bed on Sunday mornings.
items.watchOut: Love — найсильніше «подобається» (++). Українське «я люблю чай» англійською часто просто I like tea. Love кажуть, коли щось дуже-дуже подобається.

items.pattern: like sb / sth · like + -ing · Do you like …?
items.meaning: think someone or something is nice or good (+)
items.example: I **like** our new neighbours. They're very friendly.
more: Do you **like** swimming?
My dad **likes** cooking on Sundays.
items.watchOut: «Мені подобається піца» — I like pizza: на початку стоїть той, кому подобається. Не To me likes pizza. Він, вона — likes, з -s.

items.pattern: don't / doesn't like sth · don't like + -ing
items.meaning: think something is not nice (–)
items.example: I **don't like** loud music.
more: My sister **doesn't like** fish.
We **don't like** this song. Can you change it?
items.watchOut: Він, вона — doesn't like, а like без -s: She doesn't like fish. Не She don't like і не She doesn't likes.

items.pattern: hate sth · hate + -ing
items.meaning: not like something at all (– –)
items.example: I **hate** waiting for the bus in the rain.
more: My son **hates** carrots.
I **hate** cold, dark mornings.
items.watchOut: В англійській hate часто кажуть про звичайні речі: I hate Mondays — «терпіти не можу понеділків». Це не так сильно, як українське «ненавиджу».

items.pattern: be / feel happy · happy about sth · happy for sb
items.meaning: feeling good and pleased
items.example: The children were very **happy** on the first day of the holidays.
more: I'm so **happy** about my new bike!
You passed your test? I'm really **happy** for you!
items.watchOut: Радий чомусь — happy about sth: happy about the news. Радий за людину — happy for sb: I'm happy for you. Не happy for the news.

items.pattern: be / feel sad · sad about sth
items.meaning: unhappy, often because something bad happened
items.example: I always feel **sad** at the end of the summer holidays.
more: Why are you **sad**? Did something happen at school?
It's a **sad** story about a lost dog.
items.watchOut: «Мені сумно» — I'm sad, не To me is sad. «Сумувати за кимось» — miss sb: I miss you. I'm sad for you означає інше: «мені тебе шкода».

items.pattern: be / get angry · angry with sb · angry about sth
items.meaning: feeling very bad about something, so you want to shout
items.example: Mum was **angry** with us because we came home late.
more: My brother gets **angry** when he loses a game.
Why are you **angry**? What did I do?
items.watchOut: Сердитися на когось — be angry with sb (американці кажуть і angry at sb), не angry on sb. Не плутай angry (сердитий) і hungry (голодний).

items.pattern: be / get upset · upset about sth
items.meaning: unhappy and worried because something bad happened; you may cry
items.example: My little sister was **upset** when she lost her teddy bear.
more: He's **upset** about his test results.
Grandma got **upset** when she couldn't find her glasses.
items.watchOut: Наголос на другому складі: up-SET. Upset — засмучений через те, що щойно сталося: людина може навіть плакати. Sad — загальніше «сумний».

items.pattern: be / feel cold · I'm cold
items.meaning: feeling that your body is not warm enough
items.example: Put your coat on, or you'll be **cold** at the bus stop.
more: My feet are **cold**. Where are my warm socks?
The children were **cold** after swimming in the sea.
items.watchOut: «Мені холодно» — I'm cold, не It's cold to me. It's cold — про погоду чи кімнату: It's cold today. I've got a cold — «у мене застуда», це інше.

items.pattern: be / feel hot · I'm hot
items.meaning: feeling that your body is too warm
items.example: I'm really **hot**. Let's sit in the shade.
more: After the race we were all **hot** and thirsty.
I'm always **hot** at night, so I sleep with the window open.
items.watchOut: «Мені жарко» — I'm hot, не It's hot to me. It's hot — про погоду: It's hot today.

items.pattern: be / feel thirsty
items.meaning: wanting to drink something
items.example: It's a hot day and the dog is **thirsty**. Give him some water.
more: Salty crisps make me **thirsty**.
Are you **thirsty**? Have some lemonade.
items.watchOut: «Я хочу пити» — найчастіше I'm thirsty. Вимова: th — як у think, кінчик язика між зубами.

items.pattern: be / get hungry
items.meaning: wanting to eat something
items.example: There's nothing in the fridge, and I'm **hungry**!
more: Swimming always makes me **hungry**.
We were so **hungry** that we ate the whole pizza.
items.watchOut: «Я голодний» — I'm hungry (прикметник). Hunger — іменник «голод»: не I'm hunger. Не плутай з angry — «сердитий».

items.pattern: be / feel well · not feel well · very well, thanks
items.meaning: healthy, not ill
items.example: I don't feel **well**. Can I go home?
more: 'Is your grandma better?' 'Yes, she's **well** again, thanks.'
Drink lots of water and you'll soon be **well** again.
items.watchOut: Тут well означає «здоровий»: I'm well, I don't feel well (мені погано). I'm good — розмовне «у мене все гаразд»; про здоров'я краще казати well.

items.pattern: be / feel ill · be ill in bed
items.meaning: not healthy; something is wrong with your body
items.example: Our teacher is **ill**, so we've got a different teacher today.
more: I felt **ill** on the boat and couldn't eat anything.
If you feel **ill**, go and see a doctor.
items.watchOut: «Я захворів» — I'm ill (британська) або I'm sick (американська). Обережно: британське I feel sick означає «мене нудить».

items.pattern: be / feel / get tired
items.meaning: needing rest or sleep
items.example: Mum works long hours, so she's often **tired** in the evening.
more: The baby is **tired**. Let's put her to bed.
I always feel **tired** on Monday mornings.
items.watchOut: «Я втомився» — I'm tired, не I tired і не I'm tiring: tiring — те, що втомлює (a tiring day). Вимова: -ed тут не читається як окремий склад «ед».

items.pattern: be surprised · surprised to see / hear sth · surprised by sth
items.meaning: feeling something you did not expect
items.example: I was **surprised** to see my teacher at the swimming pool.
more: We were **surprised** to find a hedgehog in our garden.
Everybody was **surprised** when the quiet boy won the singing competition.
items.watchOut: Про свій стан — surprised: I was surprised. Surprising — те, що дивує: surprising news. Не I was surprising. Вимова: -ed не окремий склад.

items.pattern: prefer sth to sth · prefer + -ing to + -ing
items.meaning: like one thing more than another thing
items.uk: більше любити (щось, ніж щось); віддавати перевагу
items.example: My son **prefers** apples **to** bananas.
more: I **prefer** walking **to** going by bus.
Which do you **prefer**, tea or juice?
items.watchOut: Після prefer — to, а не than: I prefer tea to coffee. Than — після more: I like tea more than coffee. Наголос на другому складі: pre-FER.

items.pattern: hope to + verb
items.meaning: want to do something and think it is possible
items.example: I **hope to** see you at the party on Saturday.
more: We **hope to** paint the kitchen this weekend.
My brother **hopes to** play for the school team.
items.watchOut: «Сподіваюся поїхати» — I hope to go: після hope потрібне to. Не I hope go і не I hope going.

items.pattern: hope (that) + sb / sth + verb
items.meaning: want something to happen or to be true
items.example: I **hope** you like the cake. I made it myself.
more: We **hope that** you enjoy your holiday.
I **hope** the shop is still open.
items.watchOut: That часто пропускають: I hope (that) you're well. Про майбутнє після hope зазвичай present simple: I hope Dad gets home early tonight.

items.pattern: want sth · want to + verb · politer: I'd like
items.meaning: wish to have or do something
items.example: I **want** a dog for my birthday.
more: We **want to** go to the cinema tonight.
My little brother **wants** a new football.
items.watchOut: «Хочу піти» — I want to go, з to. У кафе чи магазині чемніше сказати I'd like: I'd like a hot chocolate, please. I want… там звучить різкувато.

items.pattern: want me / you / him / her / us / them to + verb
items.meaning: wish that another person does something
items.example: My mum **wants me to** tidy my room.
more: The coach **wants us to** come early on Saturday.
Grandma **wants me to** call her every Sunday.
items.watchOut: «Я хочу, щоб ти допоміг» — I want you to help, не I want that you help. Після want — me, him, her, us, them, а не I, he, she.

items.pattern: really like sth · really + verb
items.meaning: like something very much
items.example: I **really like** this café. The cakes are great.
more: My mum **really likes** old films.
We **really liked** the hotel. The pool was fantastic.
items.watchOut: «Я дуже люблю піцу» — I really like pizza або I like pizza very much. Не I very like pizza і не I like very much pizza.

items.pattern: don't like sth very much · not very much
items.meaning: not like something a lot; a soft way to say 'no'
items.example: I **don't like** rap music **very much**.
more: Tom **doesn't like** maths **very much**.
I **don't like** cold weather **very much**.
items.watchOut: Very much стоїть у кінці: I don't like it very much. Не I don't like very much it. Так звучить м'якше, ніж просто I don't like it.

items.pattern: How's your mum? · How are your parents?
items.meaning: a question: is this person OK and well?
items.example: **How's** your sister? Is she enjoying her new job?
more: '**How's** your new teacher?' 'She's really nice.'
**How are** your parents? I haven't seen them for ages.
items.watchOut: How's = How is. Про кількох людей — How are: How are your parents? Не How is your parents.

items.pattern: (And) how about you / your …?
items.meaning: a question that asks the same thing about another person
items.example: 'I'm fine, thanks. **How about** you?' 'Very well, thanks.'
more: 'My dad is fine now, thanks.' 'Good! And **how about** your mum?'
I'd like tea. **How about** you?
items.watchOut: «А ти як?» — How about you? або What about you? Не How for you?

items.pattern: a bit / a little + adjective (tired, cold, hungry…)
items.meaning: not very; only a small amount
items.example: I'm **a bit** cold. Can I borrow your jacket?
more: Grandma is **a little** tired after the long trip.
I was **a bit** surprised when he said yes.
items.watchOut: Не забувай a: a bit tired, a little tired. Bit tired без a — помилка. A lot і much перед прикметником не ставлять: не a lot tired, а very tired.

warmup.explain: «Мені холодно» — I'm cold: я + прикметник. It's cold — про погоду, а I've got a cold — «у мене застуда».

warmup.uk: Я більше люблю чай, ніж каву.
warmup.explain: Prefer A to B — з to. Than ставимо після more: I like tea more than coffee.

warmup.uk: Мама хоче, щоб я їй допоміг.
warmup.explain: Хотіти, щоб хтось щось зробив, — want sb to do sth: Mum wants me to help. Не wants that I help.
Дуже подобається — really like або like … very much. Very перед дієсловом не ставлять.

warmup.uk: Ти виграв конкурс? Я дуже радий за тебе!
warmup.q: You won the competition? I'm really happy ___ you!
warmup.explain: Радий за людину — happy for sb. Радий новині — happy about the news.
Сердитися на когось — be angry with sb (американці кажуть і at). Не on.
Трохи — a bit або a little, обов'язково з a. A few — «кілька», тільки з іменниками: a few apples.

A.q: Chocolate cake is my favourite. I ___ it!
A.explain: Улюблене — love (++). Hate і don't like означають протилежне.

A.q: I ___ tomatoes, so please don't put them in my salad.
A.explain: Не кладіть, бо не подобаються — don't like (–).

A.q: I ___ rainy days. They're the worst!
A.explain: The worst — найгірші, отже hate (– –): терпіти не можу.

B.q: Can I have some water? I'm really ___.
B.explain: Хочу пити — thirsty. Hungry — хочу їсти, tired — втомлений.

B.q: After the long walk, I was very ___.
B.explain: Про свій стан — tired. Tiring — те, що втомлює: a tiring walk.

B.q: I was ___ to get a letter from my old friend.
B.explain: Про свій стан — surprised. Surprising — те, що дивує: surprising news.

C.explain: Prefer A to B — більше любити A, ніж B. З like і want така будова з to не працює.

C.q: I ___ the bus comes soon. I'm cold!
C.explain: Сподіваюся, що… — I hope (that) … Після want потрібна інша будова: I want the bus to come.

C.q: I hope ___ my cousins next summer.
C.explain: Hope + to + дієслово: I hope to visit.

D.q: '___ your uncle?' 'Much better, thanks. He's out of hospital now.'
D.explain: Як почувається людина — How's …? (How is). What's — «що», Who's — «хто».

D.q: I'm going to the party on Saturday. ___ you?
D.explain: «А ти?» — How about you? або What about you? How for you — помилка.
«Не дуже» — not very much. Very much стоїть разом і в кінці.

example.title: A windy day at the zoo
example.uk:
У суботу ми ходили до зоопарку. Було вітряно, і мені було трохи холодно. Мій молодший брат обожнює мавп, тому ми дивилися на них цілу годину. Я не люблю змій, тому почекав на вулиці.

В обід ми були дуже голодні. Мама спитала: «Піца чи бутерброди?» Ми всі любимо піцу більше, ніж бутерброди, тому пішли в кафе.

Увечері ми були втомлені, але щасливі. Я сподіваюся поїхати туди знову наступного літа.
example.en:
On Saturday we went to the zoo. It was windy, and I was [[a bit|d5]] [[cold|b5]]. My little brother [[loves|a1]] monkeys, so we watched them for an hour. I [[don't like|a3]] snakes, so I waited outside.

At lunchtime we were very [[hungry|b8]]. Mum asked, 'Pizza or sandwiches?' We all [[prefer pizza to|c1]] sandwiches, so we went to the café.

In the evening we were [[tired|b11]] but [[happy|b1]]. I [[hope to|c2]] go there again next summer.
